entities.name: PMID:27502401
observations: 2016 RNA-seq comparison of tropical African and temperate European D. melanogaster found stronger cold-shock transcriptional responses in Africa; authors interpreted attenuated European responses as expression canalization.

About 25% of genes responded to cold shock; among 16 population-specific responses, 14 showed greater differential expression in Africa. This reflects response magnitude, not direct replicate-level expression variance.

entities.name: PMID:35380655
observations: 2022 follow-up across three pairs of populations reported regulatory evolution that can neutralize ancestral plasticity; adaptive expression changes in cold-adapted populations were more vulnerable to inbreeding perturbation, consistent with possible erosion of genetic canalization.

entities.name: Cold-response attenuation
observations: In a tropical-African versus temperate-European population RNA-seq comparison, cold-induced expression changes were generally stronger in Africa; 14 of 16 population-specific cold responses showed greater differential expression in Africa. This supports attenuated cold-shock response in temperate flies but is not a direct measure of expression variance.

entities.name: Canalization nuance
observations: A 2022 multi-population study found regulatory evolution can neutralize ancestral plasticity, while expression changes in cold-adapted populations may be more sensitive to inbreeding; canalization is one component of a broader regulatory picture.

entities.name: Cubital tunnel syndrome
observations: Ulnar-distribution paresthesias provoked by elbow flexion are consistent with cubital tunnel syndrome.

entities.name: In-situ decompression preferred
observations: For uncomplicated primary cubital tunnel syndrome refractory to conservative care, simple in-situ decompression generally achieves improvement comparable to anterior transposition with fewer complications; transposition is reserved for features such as nerve instability or specific anatomy.
